`dbreg()` runs regressions through SQL sufficient statistics and retains compact
results by default. See the README and `?dbreg` for acceleration strategies.

## Native estimators and fixest formula syntax

Use `dbreg()` for OLS/LPM and `dbglm()` for Gaussian identity (the default),
Poisson log, or binomial logit/probit/cloglog models. Supply R frames or lazy
tables with `data =`, or database `conn`/`table`/`path` arguments.

```r
fit = dbreg::dbreg(y ~ x + i(group, z, ref = "control") | firm + period,
                  conn = conn, table = "observations", weights = ~w,
                  row_id = "id", retain = "all")
fixest::coeftable(fit, cluster = ~firm + period)
predict(fit, newdata) # Regressors/FE keys only: no outcome or fitting weights.
```

Every estimator defaults to `retain = "none"`. `retain = "prediction"` saves
learned effects; `retain = "inference"` saves rows/scores for sample operations
and later covariance requests; `retain = "all"` saves both. Saving rows requires
row-sized database storage. `close(fit)` releases owned database state; cached
coefficients, covariance and likelihood survive.

### Support and differences

| Request | Supported behavior and boundary |
|---|---|
| Formula | Column main effects, ordinary interactions, `I(x^2)`/`I(x^3)`, additive/composite FEs, group intercepts/slopes `g[x]`. Slope-only `g[[x]]` is unsupported. |
| `i()` | Additive indicators or numeric/logical group slopes, evaluated/frozen `ref`/`keep` selectors, bounded fitted dictionaries. Categorical second variables, binning and surrounding interactions are unsupported. |
| Weights/offsets | Columns or one-column formulas; transformed formulas such as `~log(w)` are unsupported. |
| Subsets | Restricted predicate formulas or logical columns. Arbitrary R function evaluation and positional R vectors are unsupported. |
| Covariance | IID, HC1, and one-way clustering at fit time; retained OLS also supports two-way clustering. String/list SSC policies are shared. Later cluster columns must be in the retained original source. New external key mappings and arbitrary covariance functions are unsupported. |
| Extraction | `coef`, `vcov`, `summary`, `confint`, `logLik`, `AIC`, `BIC`, `nobs`, residuals, fitted values, `tidy`/`glance`, and the documented coefficient-table helpers. Internal fixest slots and unrelated fixest consumers are unsupported. |
| IDs | `stats::case.names()` extracts sample IDs; `df.residual()` reports residual df. The corresponding `fixest::` functions are not S3 generics and cannot dispatch to dbreg objects. |
| Prediction | Existing native OLS population intervals remain available; GLM prediction intervals and learned-FE prediction uncertainty are unsupported. R vectors preserve row order/missing positions. SQL output is a keyed relation with explicit collection. Unknown factor levels error; unknown/nonestimable absorbed-effect combinations yield missing predictions. |
| Persistence | Small learned dictionaries are portable for newdata prediction, including after release. Database dictionaries, retained rows and output handles need their live owning session and cannot be reopened by deserializing a DBI handle. |
| Large designs | One-/two-FE learned dictionaries can remain in SQL. Larger FE/varying-slope prediction systems have an explicit portable-state budget; use compact fitting when prediction recovery is unnecessary. Dense slope covariance still needs quadratic space. |

The `i()` reference and fitted coding are reused for every prediction batch.
Use `i(ref = ...)` for its references; native `factor_refs` controls ordinary
factor expansion independently of the coding inside `i()`.
`options(dbreg.i_max_columns = 1000)` bounds dictionary transfer and generated
columns. Exact BIGINT categories should be supplied as integer64/decimal strings
in R; double keys above 2^53 are rejected. Closely spaced DOUBLE categories remain
distinct even when their default printed labels coincide. First-variable SQL
types are character/enum, Boolean, DATE, DOUBLE and integers fitting signed BIGINT;
FLOAT32 and nonintegral DECIMAL categories require an explicit supported-type
conversion in the source. With no intercept, the first `i()` term keeps all levels;
later indicator terms use a reference. SQL string categories
use R collation on the bounded fitted dictionary; native DuckDB enums keep their
level order.

Delayed S3 methods support `fixest::coeftable()`, `se()`, `tstat()`, `pvalue()`
and `fixef()` on native models. `generics::augment()` explicitly collects saved
sample rows with `.fitted` and `.resid`. `tidy()` and modelsummary accept supported
covariance requests; a supplied covariance matrix is also accepted by `tidy()`.
Both packages can be attached in either order. No fixest globals are changed.
Native `dbglm()` prediction defaults to the link scale; use `type = "response"`
for means or probabilities. Models do not emulate fixest's internal structure.

## Repeated external weights

Compute each weight update outside the package and supply it to a new fit. The
sample, singleton/perfect-fit removals and weighted projections are recomputed.
The package has no outer-algorithm or EM state.

```r
for (weights in externally_computed_weights) {
  data[["current_weight"]] = weights
  fit = dbreg::dbglm(b ~ x + z | firm, data = data,
                    family = binomial("cloglog"), weights = ~current_weight)
  estimates = coef(fit)
  close(fit)
}
```

## Keyed output and lifetime

```r
output = predict(fit, conn = conn, table = "prediction_rows", row_id = "id")
head(output)                 # Bounded preview.
close(fit)                   # Output has its own resource lease.
head(output)
values = as.data.frame(output) # Explicit full collection, if desired.
close(output)
```

Caller-selected export tables and borrowed connections remain caller-owned.
Without explicit SQL source keys, retained rows receive immutable snapshot-local
keys; those keys do not assert an order on the source relation.

An executable example covering R/SQL inputs, external weights, post-fit two-way
clustering, outcome-free prediction and portable-state release is installed at:

```r
source(system.file("examples/fixest-compatibility.R", package = "dbreg"))
```

The support table above and the estimator help pages describe statistical
conventions and supported requests. OLS formulas, including supported `i()`,
factor and varying-slope terms, use `dbreg()`'s linear strategies. Retention is
opt-in; the default remains `retain = "none"`. Database work and retained SQL
storage are separate from the size of the returned R object.
